diagnostics.melting_note: The air below the clouds looks quite dry here, which is why the Modeled snow level (325 m lower than the Saturated Column estimate) looks so low: a falling snowflake in dry air loses moisture to its surroundings (sublimates) instead of warming up and melting, so it survives much closer to the ground. Once it's actually been snowing or raining for a while, that dry layer moistens up and the real snow level should sit closer to the Saturated Column number instead.
